title: Centroids, links, density, and a mixture
summary: k-means, hierarchical clustering, DBSCAN, and Gaussian mixtures.

choices.text: k-means is a centroid method. Clusters are the cells of the nearest mean, the objective is within-cluster sum of squares, and k must be chosen in advance. It prefers blobs of similar size.
DBSCAN assigns every point to exactly one cluster and has no way to call a point an outlier.

Hierarchical clustering builds a dendrogram by merging clusters (or by splitting them) under a linkage such as single, complete, average, or Ward. You can cut the tree at more than one height instead of fixing k first.
A Gaussian mixture assigns each point to exactly one component, all components share one spherical covariance, and the fit is the same hard mean update as k-means.
DBSCAN grows clusters from core points that have at least minPts neighbors inside a radius ε, and it can leave sparse points labeled as noise. Cluster shape need not be a ball, and k is not an input.
